parsed.explanation: Statutory position is favourable: same-sex conduct decriminalised (2016), and the 2024 Penal Code amendment expressly lists gender identity among protected characteristics, creating an enhanced-sentence basis for hate-motivated violence — a genuine, current, traveller-relevant protection on paper, and the only trans-specific item in the record. No documented negatives at all: no criminalisation of gender expression, no police targeting, no facility or bathroom rule, no custody-placement practice, no trans-specific violence data. Critically, however, nothing shows the protection operating — no prosecutions, no enforcement statistics, no evidence of social acceptance, and the dossier itself concedes visitor conditions may diverge from statute without saying where. Under the burden-of-proof rule a well-documented jurisdiction's silence is mildly positive, but a paper protection not shown to operate is the weakest tier of evidence. This sits below Avalet-style docs (law plus demonstrated enforcement) and above the 0.55 profiles where recurring visitor-facing refusals are actually recorded. Rating reflects a protective legal climate with unverified practice.
